quantity: Health status, in KCCQ-equivalent points: the placebo-subtracted change (higher is better), per drug class and ejection-fraction band. Rows measured on the Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire (KCCQ) carry its score type (clinical summary, overall summary, total symptom or physical limitation score); rows converted from another questionnaire, or combined from two steps, say so in the basis and in the instrument field, with the original instrument and result. A trial average, not a prediction for one patient.
method: Collected, then independently re-read and resolved by fixed rules (docs/symptom-evidence-2026-11-15/). One estimate per class and band. Minnesota Living with Heart Failure (MLHFQ) results are converted through the standardized mean difference and marked converted; a figure built from two steps is marked combined. A class with no measurement is filled from the nearest band, then a sibling class, then assumed neutral, then not measured (value 0); the basis says which. Controller ruling 2026-11-19 (round 1 review): the unit is KCCQ-equivalent points, not KCCQ points.

Original result: Minnesota Living with Heart Failure score, least-square mean change 0.19 with valsartan versus 1.94 with placebo (P = .005; lower is better), valsartan 160 mg twice daily added to background beta-blocker or ACE inhibitor therapy, average follow-up 23 months, 3,010 patients; significant on the original scale. source.trial: Beta-blocker MLHFQ pool (2 trials) in meta-analysis of HF pharmacotherapy

rows.population: HFrEF; two small trials pooled (Goldstein 1999, PMID 10577448, 38 vs 15 patients, 26 weeks; Hawkins 2009, PMID 19460848, 14 vs 13 patients, 16 weeks; about 80 patients in total)
rows.quote: No significant differences were found between beta-blockers (SMD: -0.30; 95% CI: -0.77 to 0.18; P = 0.22; I 2 = 0%) or MRA (SMD: 0.02; 95% CI: -0.13 to 0.18; P = 0.75; I 2 = 0%) and placebo groups.
rows.extrapolation: R2: standardized mean difference on MLHFQ -0.30 (negative = fewer symptoms; the source calls IV iron SMD -0.91 an improvement). KCCQ points = -(-0.30) x 21.9 = 6.57; interval -(0.18) x 21.9 = -3.94 to -(-0.77) x 21.9 = 16.86. KCCQ SD 21.9 = EMPEROR-Reduced baseline KCCQ-CSS SD.
rows.notes: NOT statistically significant in the source (SMD -0.30; 95% CI -0.77 to 0.18; P = 0.22). The converted value (0.30 x the KCCQ standard deviation 21.9) is arithmetic, not a validated crosswalk, and is about three times the sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor figure (2.14, 17,598 patients) although it rests on a result that cannot be told from no effect. Large beta-blocker outcome trials (MERIT-HF) reported only a McMaster global rating, P=0.009, no number. Weak.
